# Facts (durable memory)

Durable domain knowledge, data model, conventions, and settled decisions. The stable layer all
agents rely on. Update when a fact changes, not for daily activity.

## What AccessBuddy is
- Multi-tenant club access & credential management SaaS. Live at **https://accessbuddy.com.au**.
- Origin: rebuild of South Melbourne LSC (SMLSC) fob/building-access system (was Google Sheets +
  AppSheet + Apps Script) into a proper multi-tenant product. SMLSC is the first tenant; SMLSC's
  access hardware is **Integriti Inner Range**.
- Goal: commercialise for other surf lifesaving clubs and sports clubs.
- Business entity: Nicholas Wood Consulting Pty Ltd.

## Stack
- Frontend: Next.js (App Router). UI uses **shadcn on @base-ui/react** (NOT Radix).
- Backend: Bun + Hono. DB: Postgres (Drizzle ORM, migrations in `packages/db/drizzle`).
- Infra: GCP (Cloud Run, Cloud SQL Postgres 16), Stripe Connect, Firebase Auth, Resend (email),
  Sentry. CI/CD: GitHub Actions + release-please.

## Data model (settled)
- **Access level lives on the membership** (`tenantMemberships.accessLevelId`), NOT on the credential.
  The credential tracks status + expiry only. Integriti manages access at the member/card-holder
  level, not per-fob — a fob is just a physical token; permissions are on the person.
- Never create/deactivate credentials for an access-level change. Credential updates (expiry) use the
  `programmingRequired` flag directly on the credential, not the request pipeline.
- Orphaned-request fields exist in DB: `orphanEmail` / `orphanFirstName` / `orphanLastName`.

## Conventions (settled decisions)
- **Versioning:** `.release-please-manifest.json` is the source of truth (shown in UI footer + user
  menu). The `VERSION` file exists but is unused.
- **Branching:** `main` = production (auto-deploys), `dev` = working branch (commit here, PR to main).
- **Conventional commits matter for shipping:** release-please only cuts releases for
  `feat`/`fix`/`perf`/`revert`. `chore`/`docs`/`style`/`refactor`/`test`/`ci`/`build` merge but never
  deploy. Use `feat:`/`fix:` when a change must reach production.
- **`NEXT_PUBLIC_*` vars are Docker build args** (baked at build time), not runtime env. There are 8
  of them (see deploy workflow). Missing them → Firebase Auth / Stripe Elements / app URL silently
  undefined in the client bundle.
- **`gcloud run ... --set-env-vars` REPLACES all env vars** — use `--update-env-vars` to add one
  (replacing all once caused a prod outage).
- **base-ui Select:** render the selected label as explicit children of `SelectValue`; the
  `placeholder` prop alone won't show a selected value (common where value is a UUID).
- **Email quality:** always call `setEmailBranding()` with the tenant config before rendering any
  template; first-name-only in greetings; every email audit entry includes `subject` in metadata.
- **Stripe:** a `connect=true` webhook only receives connected-account events; platform-account

Durable domain knowledge, data model, conventions, and settled decisions. The stable layer all
agents rely on. Update when a fact changes, not for daily activity.

## What AccessBuddy is
- Multi-tenant club access & credential management SaaS. Live at **https://accessbuddy.com.au**.
- Origin: rebuild of South Melbourne LSC (SMLSC) fob/building-access system (was Google Sheets +
  AppSheet + Apps Script) into a proper multi-tenant product. SMLSC is the first tenant; SMLSC's
  access hardware is **Integriti Inner Range**.
- Goal: commercialise for other surf lifesaving clubs and sports clubs.
- Business entity: Nicholas Wood Consulting Pty Ltd.

## Stack
- Frontend: Next.js (App Router). UI uses **shadcn on @base-ui/react** (NOT Radix).
- Backend: Bun + Hono. DB: Postgres (Drizzle ORM, migrations in `packages/db/drizzle`).
- Infra: GCP (Cloud Run, Cloud SQL Postgres 16), Stripe Connect, Firebase Auth, Resend (email),
  Sentry. CI/CD: GitHub Actions + release-please.

## Data model (settled)
- **Access level lives on the membership** (`tenantMemberships.accessLevelId`), NOT on the credential.
  The credential tracks status + expiry only. Integriti manages access at the member/card-holder
  level, not per-fob — a fob is just a physical token; permissions are on the person.
- Never create/deactivate credentials for an access-level change. Credential updates (expiry) use the
  `programmingRequired` flag directly on the credential, not the request pipeline.
- Orphaned-request fields exist in DB: `orphanEmail` / `orphanFirstName` / `orphanLastName`.

- **Versioning:** `.release-please-manifest.json` is the source of truth (shown in UI footer + user
  menu). The `VERSION` file exists but is unused.
- **Branching:** `main` = production (auto-deploys), `dev` = working branch (commit here, PR to main).
- **Conventional commits matter for shipping:** release-please only cuts releases for
  `feat`/`fix`/`perf`/`revert`. `chore`/`docs`/`style`/`refactor`/`test`/`ci`/`build` merge but never
  deploy. Use `feat:`/`fix:` when a change must reach production.
- **`NEXT_PUBLIC_*` vars are Docker build args** (baked at build time), not runtime env. There are 8
  of them (see deploy workflow). Missing them → Firebase Auth / Stripe Elements / app URL silently
  undefined in the client bundle.
- **`gcloud run ... --set-env-vars` REPLACES all env vars** — use `--update-env-vars` to add one
  (replacing all once caused a prod outage).
- **base-ui Select:** render the selected label as explicit children of `SelectValue`; the
  `placeholder` prop alone won't show a selected value (common where value is a UUID).
- **Email quality:** always call `setEmailBranding()` with the tenant config before rendering any
  template; first-name-only in greetings; every email audit entry includes `subject` in metadata.

  handler trying both `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `STRIPE_PLATFORM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

Read-only code mapping, breadth "very thorough". Repo (a git worktree on latest main): /home/nicholas-wood/Documents/workspace/projects/accessbuddy/.worktrees/member-emails-merge  — a Bun/Next.js (App Router) + Drizzle/Postgres monorepo (apps/web, packages/db, packages/shared). Ignore node_modules, dist, .next, migrations-out. `fd` is not installed; use rg / find. Do not modify anything.

Context: I am designing two features: (A) a member (row in the global `users` table, packages/db/src/schema/users.ts, which today has a single `email` column) can hold multiple email addresses with one primary; (B) an admin can merge two member accounts (two `users` rows) into one. I need a complete, accurate inventory so nothing is missed. I have NOT ruled anything out yet. Report facts with file:line references; do not propose a design.

Produce these four inventories:

1. USER FOREIGN KEYS. Every table column, across packages/db/src/schema/*.ts AND packages/db/drizzle/*.sql, that references users.id or stores a user id (including nullable ones and ones without a formal FK, e.g. actor/performedBy/createdBy/approvedBy/issuedTo/holder columns, audit log actor/target ids, jsonb metadata that embeds user ids). For each: table, column, nullable?, any unique constraint or unique index involving it (give the exact constraint columns, e.g. unique(tenant_id,user_id)), and ON DELETE behaviour if specified. Also list tables with tenant_membership_id style references to tenant_memberships.id.

2. EMAIL READS/WRITES. Every place code reads or writes `users.email` or looks a user up BY email: sign-in / session creation / Firebase token verification (how is a Firebase identity mapped to a users row: by firebase_uid, by email, or both? is a users row auto-created on first sign-in? what is firebase_uid set to for admin-created or imported members who have never signed in?), magic-link / email-link sign-in flows, invites, member create/edit API routes and their zod schemas, CSV/bulk import, orphaned requests (orphanEmail) and how orphans get attached to a user, lockers "link to member", contact form, duplicate-email checks, search/filter by email in admin member lists, and any uniqueness assumption (is users.email unique in the DB? case-normalised? is there a lower() index?). Give file:line and a one-line description of each.

3. EMAIL SENDING. How outbound email picks the recipient address: the central send function(s), the email queue table and what it stores (recipient address string vs user id), and each call site category that passes user.email. I need to know whether there is a single choke point where "the member's primary email" could be resolved.

4. MEMBER ADMIN SURFACE + CONVENTIONS. (a) The admin member detail page and member edit form: file paths for the page, the form component, and the API route(s) it calls (method + path + handler file), and how permissions/roles are checked on those routes. (b) How audit log entries are written (helper name, file, signature, an example call) and where audit action labels are rendered (there are reportedly two renderers that both need a label for any new metadata.action; find both). content.content:
# Feedback (collaboration patterns / learnings)

Project-specific ways of working: what to do, what to avoid, and why. Drawn from prior sessions.

## Collaboration with Nick
- **Present the user journey before coding.** Write a 3-5 step "admin clicks X, sees Y, system does Z"
  and confirm it first. Nick thinks in UX/workflow outcomes, not implementation. Going straight to
  code caused repeated UI rework (double-click approve, missing buttons, wrong labels, edit layout).
- **Rephrase requirements as user stories.** Nick describes outcomes, not mechanisms (e.g. "split the
  pickup step" meant "set pickup location while programming, but issue separately"). Restate as
  "When [role] does [action], they should see [result]" and confirm before coding — ambiguity has
  cost three rounds of fixes.
- **Ask about edge cases and existing data state first.** Nick tests with real-ish data (bulk fobs,
  deactivated credentials, multiple roles) and surfaces issues from data state you didn't consider
  (duplicate-key constraints, stale deactivated status, permission gating). Ask: current data state?
  which roles will test? what happens to existing records?
- **Design the full lifecycle before coding incrementally.** Map the complete happy path AND edge
  cases (reassignment, deactivated fobs, no rule match, permission checks) before the first line. The
  credential add endpoint took 5+ fix rounds because each fix revealed the next gap.
- **Rebase onto main and check conflicts before opening a PR;** verify PR state before claiming it's
  updated.

## Shipping / deploy (why these bit before)
- **Use `feat:`/`fix:` (not `chore:`) when a change must reach prod.** release-please skips chore/
  docs/etc, so a chore PR merges but never deploys. (Bit during cost-opt — needed a follow-up empty
  `fix:` commit.) Pure infra/docs that don't need a deploy can stay `chore:`.
- **`gcloud run ... --set-env-vars` REPLACES all env vars — use `--update-env-vars`.** `--set` once
  wiped DATABASE_URL and caused a prod outage. When unsure, `describe` the current env first.
- **Read the FULL `terraform plan` diff before apply.** gcloud-based CI drift can roll the image back
  to `:latest` or strip env vars (`STRIPE_PLATFORM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`). Verify
  `lifecycle.ignore_changes` is still on the Cloud Run resource; add missing env vars to TF before
  applying; scope with `-target` when in doubt.
- **`NEXT_PUBLIC_*` must be Docker build args.** Missing them → Firebase Auth / Stripe Elements / app
  URL silently undefined in the client bundle (cost 30 min to trace once).

## Quality bars Nick has flagged repeatedly
- **Emails:** always `setEmailBranding()` before rendering; first-name-only greetings; test with
  tenant colours before calling an email feature done.
- **Audit log:** every email audit entry must carry `subject` in metadata, and the display must render
  it (not a bare "Email Sent").
- **base-ui Select:** render selected label as explicit children of `SelectValue` (placeholder alone
  won't show a UUID-keyed value).

## Domain gotcha
- **Access level is on the membership, not the credential.** Don't create/deactivate credentials for
  access-level changes; the programmer updates the member in Integriti, not the fob.

## Stripe
- A `connect=true` webhook misses platform-account events. A member paid $25 and the
  `payment_intent.succeeded` webhook never fired (no connected account yet), leaving the request stuck
  in `awaiting_payment`. Solution: dual webhooks with dual-secret verification.
# State (current working state)

What is in progress, the backlog, next-session intent, and active blockers. The volatile layer —

Base directory for this skill: /home/nicholas-wood/.claude/skills/ISA

## 🚨 MANDATORY: Voice Notification (REQUIRED BEFORE ANY ACTION)

**You MUST send this notification BEFORE doing anything else when this skill is invoked.**

1. **Send voice notification**:
   ```bash
   curl -s -X POST http://localhost:31337/notify \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"message": "Running the WORKFLOWNAME workflow in the ISA skill"}' \
     > /dev/null 2>&1 &
   ```

2. **Output text notification**:
   ```
   Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **ISA** skill to ACTION...
   ```

**This is not optional. Execute this curl command immediately upon skill invocation.**

# ISA — Ideal State Artifact

The ISA is the single document that articulates "done" for any thing whose ideal state we are pursuing — a project, an application, a library, infrastructure, a work session, an art piece, a strategic decision. It serves five identities simultaneously: ideal state articulation, test harness, build verification, done condition, system of record.

This skill owns the canonical template, the workflows that generate and refine ISAs, and the example library.

---

## The Twelve-Section Body (locked v6.2.0)

Every ISA may have up to twelve body sections. The tier completeness gate decides which are required at which effort tier; sections never appear empty. **Order is fixed**.

| # | Section | Purpose | Written At |
|---|---------|---------|------------|
| 1 | `## Problem` | What is broken or missing right now that makes the ideal state worth pursuing | OBSERVE |
| 2 | `## Vision` | What euphoric surprise looks like — experiential intent, 1–5 sentences | OBSERVE |
| 3 | `## Out of Scope` | Anti-vision — what is *not* included in this ideal state, declared upfront in prose | OBSERVE |
| 4 | `## Principles` | Substrate-independent truths (Deutsch reach) the work must respect | OBSERVE |
| 5 | `## Constraints` | Immovable architectural mandates that bound the solution space | OBSERVE |
| 6 | `## Goal` | The hard-to-vary spine — 1–3 sentences naming verifiable done | OBSERVE |
| 7 | `## Criteria` | Atomic ISCs (Ideal State Criteria) — one binary tool probe each, including derived `Anti:` ISCs | OBSERVE → EXECUTE |
| 8 | `## Test Strategy` | Per-ISC verification approach — `isc | type | check | threshold | tool` | OBSERVE/PLAN |
| 9 | `## Features` | Work breakdown — `name | description | satisfies: [ISC-N…] | depends_on: [feature…] | parallelizable: bool` | PLAN |
| 10 | `## Decisions` | Timestamped decision log including dead ends; `refined:` prefix for Goal/ISC restructures | any phase |
| 11 | `## Changelog` | Conjecture / refuted-by / learned / criterion-now entries — Deutsch error-correction trail | LEARN |
| 12 | `## Verification` | Evidence that each ISC passed — quoted command output, file content, screenshot path | VERIFY |

---

## Three-Guardrail Taxonomy (Principles vs Constraints vs Anti-criteria)

Adjacent concepts. Distinguished by **who they bind**.

| Guardrail | Binds | Tone | Example | Lives In |
|-----------|-------|------|---------|----------|
| **Principles** | The *thinking* | Aspirational, generalizable | "User-facing systems prioritize responsiveness." | `## Principles` |
| **Constraints** | The *solution space* | Immovable, non-negotiable | "We do not roll our own cryptography — OAuth via industry-standard libraries only." | `## Constraints` |
| **Out of Scope** | The *vision* | Declared, explicit, prose | "Mobile native apps are not part of v1." | `## Out of Scope` |
| **Anti-criteria** | The *test surface* | Granular, testable, yes/no | "Anti: /admin returns 200 in v1 build." | `## Criteria` (with `Anti:` prefix) |

The first three are author-stated (declarative). Anti-criteria are derived — they are how Out of Scope, Constraints, and Principles become probe-able.

---

## Tier Completeness Gate (HARD at all tiers)

Mirrors the v6.1.0 thinking-floor non-relaxability. Required sections per tier:

| Tier | Required Sections |
|------|-------------------|
| **E1** | Goal, Criteria |
| **E2** | Problem, Goal, Criteria, Test Strategy |
| **E3** | Problem, Vision, Out of Scope, Constraints, Goal, Criteria, Features, Test Strategy |
| **E4** | All twelve sections |
| **E5** | All twelve + active Interview workflow run before BUILD |

**Project ISA override:** any `<project>/ISA.md` requires E3+ structure regardless of the active task's tier. The project file is the long-lived source of truth; one transient E1 task must not downgrade it.

`CheckCompleteness` workflow enforces this gate. A miss blocks `phase: complete` until the missing sections are filled in.

---

## Workflow Routing

Match the verb in the request to a workflow. When ambiguous, default to Scaffold for new ISAs and CheckCompleteness for audits.

| Verb / Intent | Workflow | File |
|---------------|----------|------|
| "scaffold", "create", "generate", "new ISA from this prompt", "extract feature as ephemeral" | **Scaffold** | `Workflows/Scaffold.md` |
| "interview me", "fill in the ISA", "deepen", "ask me questions" | **Interview** | `Workflows/Interview.md` |
| "check", "audit", "score this ISA", "is it complete?" | **CheckCompleteness** | `Workflows/CheckCompleteness.md` |
| "reconcile", "merge feature file back", "ephemeral → master" | **Reconcile** | `Workflows/Reconcile.md` |
| "seed", "bootstrap from this repo", "draft an ISA from existing code" | **Seed** | `Workflows/Seed.md` |
| "append decision", "append changelog", "append verification", "record C/R/L entry" | **Append** | `Workflows/Append.md` |

**When executing a workflow, output this notification directly:**

```
Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **ISA** skill to ACTION...
```

---

## Gotchas

The highest-information-density part of this skill. Each entry captures a non-obvious failure mode that has bitten real ISA work.

- **ID-stability is the cornerstone of Reconcile — never re-number on edit.** When the Splitting Test produces a finer-grained version of `ISC-7`, preserve `ISC-7` as the parent and add `ISC-7.1`, `ISC-7.2`, etc. Even when an ISC is dropped, leave a tombstone (`- [ ] ISC-N: [DROPPED — see Decisions YYYY-MM-DD]`). Reconcile keys on stable IDs; renumbering breaks ephemeral feature-file merges silently and the failure mode looks like "the worker's checkmarks didn't land in master."
- **Ephemeral files are derived views, never sources of truth.** Scaffold's `--ephemeral` mode produces a slice of the master ISA at `MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/_ephemeral/<feature>.md`. Workers operate against that slice; Reconcile merges back. Hand-editing master content from an ephemeral file is policy-forbidden — the master is what persists; the ephemeral is what gets archived.
- **The Changelog format is non-negotiable.** Every entry needs all four pieces (`conjectured`, `refuted by`, `learned`, `criterion now`) in that order. Append refuses to write a partial C/R/L; if any of the four is missing, the entry is a Decision, not a Changelog. The format is what makes the Deutsch error-correction trail auditable across sessions.
- **Project ISAs upgrade tier to `max(declared, E3)` regardless of the active task's tier.** A `<project>/ISA.md` is the long-lived system of record for a thing with persistent identity. One transient E1 task on the project must NOT downgrade the structural minimum. CheckCompleteness applies this override automatically.
- **Empty sections never appear.** The twelve-section body is a *capacity*, not a *requirement* at every tier. Sections required-but-empty for the tier are populated; sections not required and not yet written are simply absent from the file. CheckCompleteness distinguishes `present` / `thin` / `missing` / `empty` and only `empty` is acceptable for `Verification` before VERIFY phase.
- **Anti-criteria are derived from Out of Scope plus regression-prevention concerns.** They are how the prose-guardrails (Out of Scope, Constraints, Principles) become probe-able. At least one is required at every tier; the absence of an anti-criterion at OBSERVE is a hard CheckCompleteness failure.
- **Antecedents are required when the goal is experiential.** For art, design, content, and anything that has to "land," at least one ISC must use the `Antecedent:` prefix to name a precondition that reliably produces the target experience. Verifiable goals (build, deploy, schema) don't need antecedents; experiential goals always do.
- **Reconcile is deterministic — there are no conflicts to resolve.** Either an ISC ID exists in master (mechanical merge) or it doesn't (abort with ID-stability violation). If the ephemeral made structural changes (split ISC-7 into ISC-7.1/ISC-7.2), those structural changes belong in master via a separate Edit by the user *before* Reconcile runs.
- **The format spec wins on contradiction.** `IsaFormat.md` is the file-shape contract. If this skill's prose ever drifts from the format spec, the spec is canonical and the skill updates to match — not the reverse.

---

## Examples

The `Examples/` directory holds twelve reference ISAs spanning the tier (E1–E5) × domain (code / art / design / ops / marketplace / enterprise) matrix. Always start by reading the canonical showpiece before scaffolding a new ISA — copy its section headers, then populate. Pick the example closest to your domain + scale as a template.

**Showpiece**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Examples/canonical-isa.md` | **BeanLine** — peer-to-peer specialty-coffee marketplace. The showpiece reference, fully populated across all twelve sections with real-feeling Decisions and a four-piece C/R/L Changelog. Read this first. |

**Code**

| `Examples/e5-desktop-app.md` | E5 | **WattWatch** — open-source desktop app for personal home-energy monitoring. Single-user app pattern, 50 ISCs, populated Changelog. |

**Art (experiential — antecedents required)**

| `Examples/e3-essay.md` | E3 | Write a 1500-word essay on a specific thesis. Experiential goal, antecedent ISCs, post-publish reception probes. |

**Ops**

**Enterprise**

| `Examples/e5-enterprise.md` | E5 | **Beacon Health Alliance** — multi-region HIPAA-compliant patient portal for a 50-hospital network. Compliance anti-criteria, multi-team parallelizable features, 68 ISCs across all twelve sections. |

---

## ID Stability Rule

**ISC IDs never re-number on edit.** When the Splitting Test produces a finer-grained version of `ISC-7`, the original number is preserved as the parent and children become `ISC-7.1`, `ISC-7.2`, etc. Do not collapse the numbering even if the ISC is dropped — leave a tombstone marker so historical references in Decisions, Changelog, and Verification remain valid.

This rule exists because `Reconcile` is keyed on ISC IDs. If IDs renumber across edits, ephemeral feature-file reconciliation breaks silently. The renumbering ban is what makes feature-file workflows safe.

---

## Ephemeral Feature Files (Ralph Loop / Maestro pattern)

When a feature is to be worked in an isolated context (Ralph Loop, Maestro, parallel coding-agent instances), the Algorithm invokes:

```
Skill("ISA", "extract feature <name> as ephemeral file")
```

`Scaffold` (with `--ephemeral` mode) produces a derived view at `MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/_ephemeral/<feature>.md` containing only the slice relevant to that feature: the Vision and Goal as read-only context, the relevant Constraints, the ISCs in the feature's `satisfies:` list with stable IDs, the matching Test Strategy entries, and an empty Verification section.

A fresh-context agent operates against the ephemeral file alone. At completion, `Reconcile` deterministically merges ISC checkmarks, Verification evidence, Decisions entries, and any new Changelog entries back to master, then archives the ephemeral file under `_ephemeral/.archive/`.

**Ephemeral files are derived views. They are never sources of truth. They are never hand-edited as policy. The master ISA is what persists.**

---

## Relationship to the Algorithm

The Algorithm at OBSERVE invokes this skill to scaffold or read an ISA. The skill does not run the Algorithm — it owns the artifact the Algorithm operates on.

- OBSERVE: `Skill("ISA", "scaffold from prompt at tier T")` → returns populated ISA at canonical location.
- OBSERVE: `Skill("ISA", "check completeness of <path> at tier T")` → pass/fail + gap report.
- PLAN: `Skill("ISA", "extract feature <name> as ephemeral file")` → ephemeral excerpt.
- LEARN: `Skill("ISA", "reconcile <ephemeral-path> → <master-path>")` → deterministic merge.

The Algorithm doctrine spec at `~/.claude/PAI/ALGORITHM/v6.2.0.md` (or LATEST) governs invocation cadence. This skill is invocation-agnostic — it works the same whether called by the Algorithm or directly by the user.

---

## Format spec cross-reference

The full ISA format spec lives at `~/.claude/PAI/DOCUMENTATION/IsaFormat.md`. This skill implements that spec; if there is ever a contradiction, the format spec wins and this skill is updated to match.

The system-architecture doc — five identities, three-guardrail taxonomy, twelve-section body, six workflows, two homes, subsystem relationships — lives at `~/.claude/PAI/DOCUMENTATION/Isa/IsaSystem.md`. Read that for the conceptual frame; read this file (and `IsaFormat.md`) for the operational contract.

# Feedback (collaboration patterns / learnings)

Project-specific ways of working: what to do, what to avoid, and why. Drawn from prior sessions.

## Collaboration with Nick
- **Present the user journey before coding.** Write a 3-5 step "admin clicks X, sees Y, system does Z"
  and confirm it first. Nick thinks in UX/workflow outcomes, not implementation. Going straight to
  code caused repeated UI rework (double-click approve, missing buttons, wrong labels, edit layout).
- **Rephrase requirements as user stories.** Nick describes outcomes, not mechanisms (e.g. "split the
  pickup step" meant "set pickup location while programming, but issue separately"). Restate as
  "When [role] does [action], they should see [result]" and confirm before coding — ambiguity has
  cost three rounds of fixes.
- **Ask about edge cases and existing data state first.** Nick tests with real-ish data (bulk fobs,
  deactivated credentials, multiple roles) and surfaces issues from data state you didn't consider
  (duplicate-key constraints, stale deactivated status, permission gating). Ask: current data state?
  which roles will test? what happens to existing records?
- **Design the full lifecycle before coding incrementally.** Map the complete happy path AND edge
  cases (reassignment, deactivated fobs, no rule match, permission checks) before the first line. The
  credential add endpoint took 5+ fix rounds because each fix revealed the next gap.
- **Rebase onto main and check conflicts before opening a PR;** verify PR state before claiming it's
  updated.

## Shipping / deploy (why these bit before)
- **Use `feat:`/`fix:` (not `chore:`) when a change must reach prod.** release-please skips chore/
  docs/etc, so a chore PR merges but never deploys. (Bit during cost-opt — needed a follow-up empty
  `fix:` commit.) Pure infra/docs that don't need a deploy can stay `chore:`.
- **`gcloud run ... --set-env-vars` REPLACES all env vars — use `--update-env-vars`.** `--set` once
  wiped DATABASE_URL and caused a prod outage. When unsure, `describe` the current env first.
- **Read the FULL `terraform plan` diff before apply.** gcloud-based CI drift can roll the image back
  to `:latest` or strip env vars (`STRIPE_PLATFORM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`). Verify
  `lifecycle.ignore_changes` is still on the Cloud Run resource; add missing env vars to TF before
  applying; scope with `-target` when in doubt.
- **`NEXT_PUBLIC_*` must be Docker build args.** Missing them → Firebase Auth / Stripe Elements / app
  URL silently undefined in the client bundle (cost 30 min to trace once).

## Quality bars Nick has flagged repeatedly
- **Emails:** always `setEmailBranding()` before rendering; first-name-only greetings; test with
  tenant colours before calling an email feature done.
- **Audit log:** every email audit entry must carry `subject` in metadata, and the display must render
  it (not a bare "Email Sent").
- **base-ui Select:** render selected label as explicit children of `SelectValue` (placeholder alone
  won't show a UUID-keyed value).

## Domain gotcha
- **Access level is on the membership, not the credential.** Don't create/deactivate credentials for
  access-level changes; the programmer updates the member in Integriti, not the fob.

## Stripe
- A `connect=true` webhook misses platform-account events. A member paid $25 and the
  `payment_intent.succeeded` webhook never fired (no connected account yet), leaving the request stuck
  in `awaiting_payment`. Solution: dual webhooks with dual-secret verification.

# ISA — Ideal State Artifact

The ISA is the single document that articulates "done" for any thing whose ideal state we are pursuing — a project, an application, a library, infrastructure, a work session, an art piece, a strategic decision. It serves five identities simultaneously: ideal state articulation, test harness, build verification, done condition, system of record.

This skill owns the canonical template, the workflows that generate and refine ISAs, and the example library.

---

## The Twelve-Section Body (locked v6.2.0)

Every ISA may have up to twelve body sections. The tier completeness gate decides which are required at which effort tier; sections never appear empty. **Order is fixed**.

| # | Section | Purpose | Written At |
|---|---------|---------|------------|
| 1 | `## Problem` | What is broken or missing right now that makes the ideal state worth pursuing | OBSERVE |
| 2 | `## Vision` | What euphoric surprise looks like — experiential intent, 1–5 sentences | OBSERVE |
| 3 | `## Out of Scope` | Anti-vision — what is *not* included in this ideal state, declared upfront in prose | OBSERVE |
| 4 | `## Principles` | Substrate-independent truths (Deutsch reach) the work must respect | OBSERVE |
| 5 | `## Constraints` | Immovable architectural mandates that bound the solution space | OBSERVE |
| 6 | `## Goal` | The hard-to-vary spine — 1–3 sentences naming verifiable done | OBSERVE |
| 7 | `## Criteria` | Atomic ISCs (Ideal State Criteria) — one binary tool probe each, including derived `Anti:` ISCs | OBSERVE → EXECUTE |
| 8 | `## Test Strategy` | Per-ISC verification approach — `isc | type | check | threshold | tool` | OBSERVE/PLAN |
| 9 | `## Features` | Work breakdown — `name | description | satisfies: [ISC-N…] | depends_on: [feature…] | parallelizable: bool` | PLAN |
| 10 | `## Decisions` | Timestamped decision log including dead ends; `refined:` prefix for Goal/ISC restructures | any phase |
| 11 | `## Changelog` | Conjecture / refuted-by / learned / criterion-now entries — Deutsch error-correction trail | LEARN |
| 12 | `## Verification` | Evidence that each ISC passed — quoted command output, file content, screenshot path | VERIFY |

---

## Three-Guardrail Taxonomy (Principles vs Constraints vs Anti-criteria)

Adjacent concepts. Distinguished by **who they bind**.

| Guardrail | Binds | Tone | Example | Lives In |
|-----------|-------|------|---------|----------|
| **Principles** | The *thinking* | Aspirational, generalizable | "User-facing systems prioritize responsiveness." | `## Principles` |
| **Constraints** | The *solution space* | Immovable, non-negotiable | "We do not roll our own cryptography — OAuth via industry-standard libraries only." | `## Constraints` |
| **Out of Scope** | The *vision* | Declared, explicit, prose | "Mobile native apps are not part of v1." | `## Out of Scope` |
| **Anti-criteria** | The *test surface* | Granular, testable, yes/no | "Anti: /admin returns 200 in v1 build." | `## Criteria` (with `Anti:` prefix) |

The first three are author-stated (declarative). Anti-criteria are derived — they are how Out of Scope, Constraints, and Principles become probe-able.

---

## Tier Completeness Gate (HARD at all tiers)

Mirrors the v6.1.0 thinking-floor non-relaxability. Required sections per tier:

| Tier | Required Sections |
|------|-------------------|
| **E1** | Goal, Criteria |
| **E2** | Problem, Goal, Criteria, Test Strategy |
| **E3** | Problem, Vision, Out of Scope, Constraints, Goal, Criteria, Features, Test Strategy |
| **E4** | All twelve sections |
| **E5** | All twelve + active Interview workflow run before BUILD |

**Project ISA override:** any `<project>/ISA.md` requires E3+ structure regardless of the active task's tier. The project file is the long-lived source of truth; one transient E1 task must not downgrade it.

`CheckCompleteness` workflow enforces this gate. A miss blocks `phase: complete` until the missing sections are filled in.

---

## Workflow Routing

Match the verb in the request to a workflow. When ambiguous, default to Scaffold for new ISAs and CheckCompleteness for audits.

| Verb / Intent | Workflow | File |
|---------------|----------|------|
| "scaffold", "create", "generate", "new ISA from this prompt", "extract feature as ephemeral" | **Scaffold** | `Workflows/Scaffold.md` |
| "interview me", "fill in the ISA", "deepen", "ask me questions" | **Interview** | `Workflows/Interview.md` |
| "check", "audit", "score this ISA", "is it complete?" | **CheckCompleteness** | `Workflows/CheckCompleteness.md` |
| "reconcile", "merge feature file back", "ephemeral → master" | **Reconcile** | `Workflows/Reconcile.md` |
| "seed", "bootstrap from this repo", "draft an ISA from existing code" | **Seed** | `Workflows/Seed.md` |
| "append decision", "append changelog", "append verification", "record C/R/L entry" | **Append** | `Workflows/Append.md` |

**When executing a workflow, output this notification directly:**

```
Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **ISA** skill to ACTION...
```

---

## Gotchas

The highest-information-density part of this skill. Each entry captures a non-obvious failure mode that has bitten real ISA work.

- **ID-stability is the cornerstone of Reconcile — never re-number on edit.** When the Splitting Test produces a finer-grained version of `ISC-7`, preserve `ISC-7` as the parent and add `ISC-7.1`, `ISC-7.2`, etc. Even when an ISC is dropped, leave a tombstone (`- [ ] ISC-N: [DROPPED — see Decisions YYYY-MM-DD]`). Reconcile keys on stable IDs; renumbering breaks ephemeral feature-file merges silently and the failure mode looks like "the worker's checkmarks didn't land in master."
- **Ephemeral files are derived views, never sources of truth.** Scaffold's `--ephemeral` mode produces a slice of the master ISA at `MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/_ephemeral/<feature>.md`. Workers operate against that slice; Reconcile merges back. Hand-editing master content from an ephemeral file is policy-forbidden — the master is what persists; the ephemeral is what gets archived.
- **The Changelog format is non-negotiable.** Every entry needs all four pieces (`conjectured`, `refuted by`, `learned`, `criterion now`) in that order. Append refuses to write a partial C/R/L; if any of the four is missing, the entry is a Decision, not a Changelog. The format is what makes the Deutsch error-correction trail auditable across sessions.
- **Project ISAs upgrade tier to `max(declared, E3)` regardless of the active task's tier.** A `<project>/ISA.md` is the long-lived system of record for a thing with persistent identity. One transient E1 task on the project must NOT downgrade the structural minimum. CheckCompleteness applies this override automatically.
- **Empty sections never appear.** The twelve-section body is a *capacity*, not a *requirement* at every tier. Sections required-but-empty for the tier are populated; sections not required and not yet written are simply absent from the file. ## ID Stability Rule

**ISC IDs never re-number on edit.** When the Splitting Test produces a finer-grained version of `ISC-7`, the original number is preserved as the parent and children become `ISC-7.1`, `ISC-7.2`, etc. Do not collapse the numbering even if the ISC is dropped — leave a tombstone marker so historical references in Decisions, Changelog, and Verification remain valid.

This rule exists because `Reconcile` is keyed on ISC IDs. If IDs renumber across edits, ephemeral feature-file reconciliation breaks silently. The renumbering ban is what makes feature-file workflows safe.

---

## Ephemeral Feature Files (Ralph Loop / Maestro pattern)

When a feature is to be worked in an isolated context (Ralph Loop, Maestro, parallel coding-agent instances), the Algorithm invokes:

```
Skill("ISA", "extract feature <name> as ephemeral file")
```

`Scaffold` (with `--ephemeral` mode) produces a derived view at `MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/_ephemeral/<feature>.md` containing only the slice relevant to that feature: the Vision and Goal as read-only context, the relevant Constraints, the ISCs in the feature's `satisfies:` list with stable IDs, the matching Test Strategy entries, and an empty Verification section.

A fresh-context agent operates against the ephemeral file alone. At completion, `Reconcile` deterministically merges ISC checkmarks, Verification evidence, Decisions entries, and any new Changelog entries back to master, then archives the ephemeral file under `_ephemeral/.archive/`.

**Ephemeral files are derived views. They are never sources of truth. They are never hand-edited as policy. The master ISA is what persists.**

# 2. EMAIL READS/WRITES

## 2a. Uniqueness and normalisation facts
- `users.email` is `text NOT NULL` with **no unique constraint and no index of any kind** (users.ts:7; 0000:18). I checked every migration: none alter or index `users.email`.
- The code says outright that it is not unique: lib/services/locker-core.ts:304 ("users.email is not unique; when several accounts share an email the earliest-created one with a membership wins").
- There are three separate normalise helpers, all `toLowerCase().trim()`:
  - lib/member-update-diff.ts:56
  - lib/services/locker-core.ts:68 (re-exported from lockers.ts)
  - lib/otp-store.ts:25
- Nearly all lookups are **exact `eq(users.email, x)` with `.limit(1)` and no ORDER BY**, so the result is non-deterministic if duplicates exist. The only case-insensitive lookups are in the lockers code (`lower(users.email)`).

## 2b. Sign-in and session

**Firebase identity → `users` row.** `getAuthUser` (lib/auth.ts:134-284) does this:
- Decodes the cookie. For Firebase cookies the email is lower-cased and trimmed at 182 and 193; for webauthn./OTP cookies at 90.
- **Looks up by `firebase_uid` first** (204-208).
- **If not found and an email exists, falls back to `eq(users.email, email)`** (210-216). On a match it **overwrites `firebase_uid` with the real uid** and, from displayName, first/last name (218-228).
- **If there is still no row, it auto-creates a users row** (230-245) with `onConflictDoUpdate` on firebaseUid that sets email (241-244). So yes, a row is auto-created on first sign-in.
- **On every request it attaches orphans:** `UPDATE fob_requests SET requester_id = user.id WHERE orphan_email = user.email AND requester_id IS NULL` (252-261). This is an exact match, not lower(). If the user has no name, it backfills from the orphan's name (264-276).
- `buildAuthContext` (299-349) exposes `user.email` = `users.email`.

# 3. EMAIL SENDING

**Central functions** (lib/services/email.ts):
- `sendEmail(to: string, subject, html, config, attachments?, audit?, templateType?)` at 215 is the only Resend call (261), apart from the contact route. It writes `email_sent`/`email_failed` audits with `metadata.to` (321-374).
- `sendTemplatedEmail(to: string, templateType, variables, config, attachments?, audit?)` at 556.
- `sendAdminNotification(tx, {tenantId, requiredPermission, …})` at 909. **This one takes ids, not an address:** it resolves admin user ids from admin_assignments, then `users.email` (982-985).
- `sendDailySummaryEmails` at 1095 resolves `users.email` for admins (1282-1284, send at 1388).
- **Every member-facing function takes a ready-made address string.** None accepts a user id.

**Queue** (`email_queue`, email-queue.ts):
- Stores **`recipient: text` (the address string)**, payload, entity_type/entity_id. It does not store a user id.
- `enqueueEmail(tx, {recipient, …})` at lib/services/email-queue.ts:142.
- The drain sends to `row.recipient` (283-284).
- The address is frozen at enqueue time.

**Where each call site gets its address:**

| Source of address | Call sites |
|---|---|
| `users.email` resolved from `requester_id`, falling back to `orphan_email` | `notifyRequestEvent`-style block in lib/services/requests.ts:1771-1788, which covers ~20 template sends at 1839-2176. Also requests.ts:2490-2502 and 2528 (paymentRequired), cron/daily/route.ts:637-651 (paymentReminder, sent at 675) and 837-851 (pickupReminder, sent at 893). |
| `users.email` by requester_id | requests.ts:1317-1338 (refund), 1440-1473 (deactivated); requests/[id]/refund/route.ts:125-147 |
| `users.email` by credential owner_id | credentials/route.ts:602-690; credentials/[id]/confirm-programming:119-150; credentials/[id]/revoke:146-167; cron/daily:530-551 and 749-769 (enqueued) |
| `users.email` by user id (member routes) | members/[id]/renew:91-99; members/[id]/resend-attestation:94-137; members/[id]/archive:73-91; cron/daily:315-429 (attestations, enqueued) |
| Typed/form address (not users.email) | magic-link.ts:58,78; send-otp:98,116; send-code:69; requests/submit:279,641 (`data.email`) |
| Locker snapshot columns | `sendMemberLockerEmail({to})` (locker-core.ts:131-160). Callers pass `request.email` (lockers.ts:612, 839), `done.member.email` from users (783, 1011), `holder_email` (1072, 1208; locker-season.ts:655), and enqueue with `ended.holderEmail` (locker-season.ts:386-389). |

**Choke point:** every send goes through `sendEmail(to: string)`, but that is too late to choose an address: by then `to` is already a string. There is **no shared "resolve a member's recipient" helper**. About 15 files each select `users.email` themselves. Two partial resolvers exist:
- the requests.ts notify block (1771-1788)
- the user-id-to-email lookup inside `sendAdminNotification` (email.ts:982).

Queued rows and locker snapshots carry addresses frozen at write time.

- The code says outright that it is not unique: lib/services/locker-core.ts:304 ("users.email is not unique; when several accounts share an email the earliest-created one with a membership wins").
- There are three separate normalise helpers, all `toLowerCase().trim()`:
  - lib/member-update-diff.ts:56
  - lib/services/locker-core.ts:68 (re-exported from lockers.ts)
  - lib/otp-store.ts:25
- Nearly all lookups are **exact `eq(users.email, x)` with `.limit(1)` and no ORDER BY**, so the result is non-deterministic if duplicates exist. The only case-insensitive lookups are in the lockers code (`lower(users.email)`).

## 2a. Uniqueness and normalisation facts
- `users.email` is `text NOT NULL` with **no unique constraint and no index of any kind** (users.ts:7; 0000:18). I checked every migration: none alter or index `users.email`.
- The code says outright that it is not unique: lib/services/locker-core.ts:304 ("users.email is not unique; when several accounts share an email the earliest-created one with a membership wins").
- There are three separate normalise helpers, all `toLowerCase().trim()`:
  - lib/member-update-diff.ts:56
  - lib/services/locker-core.ts:68 (re-exported from lockers.ts)
  - lib/otp-store.ts:25
- Nearly all lookups are **exact `eq(users.email, x)` with `.limit(1)` and no ORDER BY**, so the result is non-deterministic if duplicates exist. The only case-insensitive lookups are in the lockers code (`lower(users.email)`).

## 2b. Sign-in and session

**Firebase identity → `users` row.** `getAuthUser` (lib/auth.ts:134-284) does this:
- Decodes the cookie. For Firebase cookies the email is lower-cased and trimmed at 182 and 193; for webauthn./OTP cookies at 90.
- **Looks up by `firebase_uid` first** (204-208).
- **If not found and an email exists, falls back to `eq(users.email, email)`** (210-216). On a match it **overwrites `firebase_uid` with the real uid** and, from displayName, first/last name (218-228).
- **If there is still no row, it auto-creates a users row** (230-245) with `onConflictDoUpdate` on firebaseUid that sets email (241-244). So yes, a row is auto-created on first sign-in.
- **On every request it attaches orphans:** `UPDATE fob_requests SET requester_id = user.id WHERE orphan_email = user.email AND requester_id IS NULL` (252-261). This is an exact match, not lower(). If the user has no name, it backfills from the orphan's name (264-276).
- `buildAuthContext` (299-349) exposes `user.email` = `users.email`.

# 3. EMAIL SENDING

**Central functions** (lib/services/email.ts):
- `sendEmail(to: string, subject, html, config, attachments?, audit?, templateType?)` at 215 is the only Resend call (261), apart from the contact route. It writes `email_sent`/`email_failed` audits with `metadata.to` (321-374).
- `sendTemplatedEmail(to: string, templateType, variables, config, attachments?, audit?)` at 556.
- `sendAdminNotification(tx, {tenantId, requiredPermission, …})` at 909. **This one takes ids, not an address:** it resolves admin user ids from admin_assignments, then `users.email` (982-985).
- `sendDailySummaryEmails` at 1095 resolves `users.email` for admins (1282-1284, send at 1388).
- **Every member-facing function takes a ready-made address string.** None accepts a user id.

**Queue** (`email_queue`, email-queue.ts):
- Stores **`recipient: text` (the address string)**, payload, entity_type/entity_id. It does not store a user id.
- `enqueueEmail(tx, {recipient, …})` at lib/services/email-queue.ts:142.
- The drain sends to `row.recipient` (283-284).
- The address is frozen at enqueue time.

**Where each call site gets its address:**

| Source of address | Call sites |
|---|---|
| `users.email` resolved from `requester_id`, falling back to `orphan_email` | `notifyRequestEvent`-style block in lib/services/requests.ts:1771-1788, which covers ~20 template sends at 1839-2176. Also requests.ts:2490-2502 and 2528 (paymentRequired), cron/daily/route.ts:637-651 (paymentReminder, sent at 675) and 837-851 (pickupReminder, sent at 893). |
| `users.email` by requester_id | requests.ts:1317-1338 (refund), 1440-1473 (deactivated); requests/[id]/refund/route.ts:125-147 |
| `users.email` by credential owner_id | credentials/route.ts:602-690; credentials/[id]/confirm-programming:119-150; credentials/[id]/revoke:146-167; cron/daily:530-551 and 749-769 (enqueued) |
| `users.email` by user id (member routes) | members/[id]/renew:91-99; members/[id]/resend-attestation:94-137; members/[id]/archive:73-91; cron/daily:315-429 (attestations, enqueued) |
| Typed/form address (not users.email) | magic-link.ts:58,78; send-otp:98,116; send-code:69; requests/submit:279,641 (`data.email`) |
| Locker snapshot columns | `sendMemberLockerEmail({to})` (locker-core.ts:131-160). Callers pass `request.email` (lockers.ts:612, 839), `done.member.email` from users (783, 1011), `holder_email` (1072, 1208; locker-season.ts:655), and enqueue with `ended.holderEmail` (locker-season.ts:386-389). |

**Choke point:** every send goes through `sendEmail(to: string)`, but that is too late to choose an address: by then `to` is already a string. There is **no shared "resolve a member's recipient" helper**. About 15 files each select `users.email` themselves. Two partial resolvers exist:
- the requests.ts notify block (1771-1788)
- the user-id-to-email lookup inside `sendAdminNotification` (email.ts:982).

Queued rows and locker snapshots carry addresses frozen at write time.

  - Journal `when` values for recent entries are hand-picked round numbers. 0021:9-10 says "If main gains another migration first, renumber this file, its journal entry and the tag."
- **Last two `_journal.json` entries:**
  ```json
  { "idx": 20, "version": "7", "when": 1786000000000, "tag": "0020_attestation_requests_credential_ids", "breakpoints": true },
  { "idx": 21, "version": "7", "when": 1786000060000, "tag": "0021_lockers", "breakpoints": true }
  ```
- `migrate.ts` runs the drizzle `migrate()`, then `verify-migrations.ts`. That regex-parses CREATE/DROP/RENAME TABLE across the journal and exits 1 if any expected table is missing.
- **`apps/web/src/__tests__/schema-parity.test.ts`** (runs only with DATABASE_URL) checks against a freshly migrated DB:
  - every ORM table exists (69-84)
  - every ORM column exists (86-107)
  - every column's **nullability matches** the ORM (109-144)
- **`packages/db/src/check-schema-drift.ts`** runs drizzle-kit `pushSchema` as a dry-run planner against the migrated DB and classifies statements:
  - FATAL (exit 1): `CREATE …`, `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN`, `DROP TABLE`
  - IGNORED: `DROP POLICY`, `DROP INDEX`, `DISABLE/NO FORCE RLS`
  - WARN: everything else, e.g. constraint-name churn, defaults, nullability
  - Per 0021:74-77, expression indexes like `lower(email)` are avoided because they break this introspection.

## (e) Tests and commands
- Vitest everywhere:
  - `apps/web/vitest.config.ts`: globals, `@` alias to `./src`, vitest ^4
  - `packages/db/vitest.config.ts` (vitest ^3)
  - `packages/shared/vitest.config.ts`
- **There is no embedded Postgres harness.** DB tests are gated on `DATABASE_URL` (`describe.skipIf(!hasDb)` or `describeIfDb`) and run against a real Postgres:
  - CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml): `postgres:16` service container (`accessbuddy`/`testpassword`/`accessbuddy_test`) plus redis:7. Steps: `bun run db:migrate` → `bun run db:check-drift` → `bun run test`.
  - Locally: `docker-compose.yml` has `postgres:16-alpine` on 5432 (`accessbuddy`/`accessbuddy`/`accessbuddy`).
  - Turbo passes `DATABASE_URL` and `REDIS_URL` through to `test`.
- 18 DB-gated test files in apps/web/src/__tests__. They insert synthetic tenants and users and clean up after themselves (`helpers/locker-fixture.ts`: mkTenant, mkUser, addMembership, addAdmin, cleanup).
- **Route-test pattern:**
  - Import the route handler directly and call it with `new NextRequest(...)` and `{ params: Promise.resolve({...}) }`.
  - Mock `next/headers` cookies to return `dev_login_email` so real `getAuthUser`/`buildAuthContext` runs.
  - Mock `@/lib/services/email` sends.
  - Example: `apps/web/src/__tests__/lockers-routes.test.ts:1-110`.
  - Member-route examples: `force-renew.test.ts` (imports `members/[id]/force-renew/route` at 256), `manual-add-expiry-update.test.ts` (cancel-confirmation and confirm-on-behalf routes at 369-372), `tenant-isolation.test.ts` (members GET at 163).
- **Commands** (repo root, Bun 1.3.11 + Turbo):
  - typecheck: `bun run typecheck` (per package `tsc --noEmit`)
  - lint: `bun run lint` (per package `eslint src/`)
  - test: `bun run test` (per package `vitest run`); DB tests need `DATABASE_URL` plus a prior `bun run db:migrate`
  - drift: `bun run db:check-drift`
  - CI also runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and `bun run build`

- Any unique constraint, `lower()` index or citext on `users.email`.
- Any code path that deletes a `users` row.
- Any merge or dedupe utility for users.
- A PATCH handler for `/api/v1/auth/me`, which the member profile form calls.

- A FK on `platform_settings.updated_by`.

- Any CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md in the repo.
- Email matching in reconciliation (it matches by name and serial only).

Uncertain items I included anyway:
- `email_queue.entity_id` storing a user id under the CREDENTIAL entity type (cron/daily:423).

lastPrompt: IN access buddy, can we have the ability to have multiple emails against a memeber, with one selected as primary. Also the ability to merge two member accounts together.

content.text:
The inventory is back and it shapes the design. The findings that matter: `users.email` has no uniqueness or index and is looked up by exact match in about 20 places; `users.id` is referenced by roughly 30 columns plus the audit log's member entries; sign-in maps a Firebase identity to a member by Firebase ID then by email, and auto-creates a new member when neither matches (which is how duplicates arise); no code deletes or merges users today.

━━━ 🧠 THINK ━━━ 2/7

🎲 RISKIEST ASSUMPTIONS: a second address should also sign the member in and match their requests (otherwise duplicates keep appearing); merge is single-club only for now; merge is irreversible so it needs a preview and explicit confirmation.
⚰️ PREMORTEM: a missed user reference strands data or blocks the delete; a new unique rule on email fails on existing duplicate rows in production; a merged member can no longer sign in; two memberships in the same club collide.
☑️ PREREQUISITES CHECK: local Postgres needed for the DB-gated tests; checking now, and taking the design to the advisor before building.

input.command:
cd ~/.claude && timeout 240 bun PAI/TOOLS/Inference.ts --mode advisor \
"TASK: AccessBuddy (live multi-tenant Next.js/Drizzle/Postgres club access SaaS, one live tenant, ~192 members). Add (A) multiple emails per member with one primary and (B) admin merge of two member accounts (two rows in the GLOBAL users table)." \
"STATE: users(id, firebase_uid UNIQUE NOT NULL, email text NOT NULL with NO unique/index; duplicates may exist in prod). ~350 code reads of users.email; ~20 lookups by exact eq(users.email). ~30 columns FK users.id (mostly ON DELETE no action) incl tenant_memberships UNIQUE(tenant_id,user_id), admin_assignments UNIQUE(tenant_id,user_id), notification_preferences UNIQUE(tenant_id,user_id,type), audit_log.actor_id, plus audit_log.entity_id (no FK) when entity_type=member. Sign-in: lookup by firebase_uid, fallback eq(users.email) then overwrite firebase_uid, else AUTO-CREATE a users row (source of duplicates). OTP/webauthn sessions sign with users.firebase_uid. RLS policies exist but prod role currently bypasses; users table has no RLS. PROPOSED DESIGN: (A) keep users.email as THE primary (no change to 350 reads); new global table user_alternate_emails(id, user_id FK cascade, email lower-cased UNIQUE, firebase_uid UNIQUE NULL, created_by, created_at). App-level check that an alternate is not another user's primary (error offers merge). Make-primary = transactional swap of users.email<->alternate row incl firebase uids. One helper findUserByEmail (primary first, then alternate) replaces the ~20 lookups (sign-in, OTP, request submit, orphan attach, lockers resolve, manual add dup check, member search). Outbound mail still goes to primary only. (B) merge = single transaction: resolve unique collisions (membership: keep target, OR the role flags, fill nulls; admin_assignment: union permissions; notification prefs: keep target), repoint every user FK + audit member entity_id + audit actor_id to target, move source primary+alternates to target alternates (with source firebase_uid attached to its email row), fill blank profile fields, write member_merged audit with full source snapshot, DELETE source users row. Guards: not self, source != acting admin, refuse if either user has membership/admin role in another tenant, permission MANAGE_ADMINS, preview endpoint + type-to-confirm UI. Test introspects information_schema FKs to users.id and fails if merge does not cover one. Ship as branch + PR only; migration is additive (one new table)." \
"QUESTION: Before I build: is alternates-table-plus-users.email-as-primary the right model versus a full user_emails table with is_primary? Is repoint-and-delete right versus tombstoning the source row? What failure modes or missed cases would you flag (auth, audit integrity, concurrency, RLS cutover, in-flight requests/attestations/payments)? Be concrete and brief." 2>&1 | tail -70

content.content:
**Repoint-and-delete is right, and the `ON DELETE no action` FKs are a free completeness check.** A missed reference makes the `DELETE` fail and the whole transaction rolls back. A tombstone loses that check and leaves a ghost row in about 350 readers.

**Add a tiny `user_merges(source_id PK, target_id, merged_at, merged_by)` redirect table.** Stale references to the source id will arrive from outside the database:

- Stripe PaymentIntent metadata.
- Links in emails already sent.
- Attestation and confirmation tokens (migration 0020).
- Session payloads.

Webhooks and token handlers must resolve through it. Otherwise a source user's in-flight payment hits "user not found" after the merge. Given the `paidAt`-is-a-cache history, that is exactly where money gets lost.

## 3. Failure modes and missed cases

**Security (biggest):**

- **Alternate email is a login credential.** A tenant admin adding an alternate is effectively assigning someone sign-in access to that member's account.
  - Require OTP verification of the new address before it can authenticate. Alternatively, store it unverified and exclude it from auth lookups until verified.
  - Admin-added and unverified is fine for request matching. It is not fine for sign-in.
- **The "already another user's primary, offer merge" error leaks across tenants.** It reveals that the address exists anywhere in the system.
  - Only reveal the collision or offer merge if the other user is exclusively in the same tenant.
  - Otherwise return a generic refusal.

**FK coverage gaps your test won't catch:**

- **Non-FK user references.** `audit_log.entity_id` is not the only one. Look for user ids or member ids inside JSONB (audit metadata, notification payloads, event rows, locker imports, request snapshots).
  - Grep for `userId`/`memberId` in JSON writes.
  - Have the test also flag uuid columns named `*user_id`/`*member_id` that lack an FK.
- **Unique indexes, not just FKs.** Introspect `pg_index`, including partial indexes such as "one open request per user" or "one active credential per user per tenant".
  - Each one needs an explicit collision rule.
  - Otherwise the repoint `UPDATE` throws mid-transaction on real data.

**Membership merge semantics:**

- "Keep target, fill nulls" silently drops conflicting fields: status, membership number, expiry, `member_message`, fob or credential state.
- The preview must show field-level conflicts and let the admin pick, or at least show what is discarded.
- Flag in the preview if the merge grants admin permissions the target didn't have.

**Concurrency:**

- `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` both users rows, ordered by id, to avoid deadlock.
- A concurrent insert referencing the source (a request submit, or the source signing in) between repoint and delete will make the delete fail and roll back. That's good, but surface a "retry" message rather than a 500.
- Source sessions after the merge: decide explicitly. Either resolve via the alternate uid, or force a logout.

**Audit integrity:**

- Rewriting `actor_id`/`entity_id` rewrites history.
- Record the rewritten audit row ids, or counts per table, in the `member_merged` event so it is reconstructible.
- The full source snapshot is good. Include alternates and `firebase_uid`.

**RLS cutover:**

- Sign-in and `findUserByEmail` run before tenant context exists, so the global alternates table needs a privileged path when `accessbuddy_app` stops bypassing RLS.
- Merge touches tables across the whole schema. Run it on an explicit privileged connection and document it in the cutover checklist alongside the cron bare-db risk.

**Stripe and external IDs:**

- If both users have Stripe customer ids or similar, keep the target's.
- Record the source's in the snapshot. Don't drop it silently.

## Verdict

Proceed with the alternates model and repoint-and-delete, plus:

- the `user_merges` redirect table;
- no uid swap on make-primary;
- verification before an alternate can authenticate;
- a tenant-scoped collision error;
- unique-index introspection, not just FKs.

Branch and PR only is right. Run the duplicate-email and unique-index reports against prod read-only before writing the collision rules.

mkdir -p "$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp" && cat > "$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/isa-add.ts" <<'EOF'
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "fs";
const p = `${process.env.HOME}/Documents/workspace/projects/accessbuddy/ISA.md`;
let s = readFileSync(p, "utf8");
const crit = `
### Member emails and member merge (2026-11-22, branch \`feat/member-emails-and-merge\`; spec in Decisions)
- [ ] ISC-269: Migration 0022 creates \`user_alternate_emails\` (user FK cascade, unique lower-cased email, nullable unique firebase uid) and is listed in the journal
- [ ] ISC-270: Migration 0022 creates \`user_merges\` (source id primary key, target id, merged at, merged by)
- [ ] ISC-271: Anti: migration 0022 adds no constraint or index to \`users.email\`, so existing duplicate rows cannot fail the deploy
- [ ] ISC-272: Schema parity and drift checks pass on a database migrated through 0022
- [ ] ISC-273: \`findUserByEmail\` returns the member whose primary matches, else the member holding the address as an additional email, case-insensitively
- [ ] ISC-274: An admin with the member-edit permission can add an additional email to a member
- [ ] ISC-275: Adding an invalid address, or one the member already holds, is rejected with a 400
- [ ] ISC-276: Adding an address held by another member of the same club is rejected with a 409 that names that member so the admin can merge
- [ ] ISC-277: Anti: adding an address held only by a member of another club returns a generic refusal that reveals no name
- [ ] ISC-278: An admin can remove an additional email
- [ ] ISC-279: Anti: the primary email cannot be removed
- [ ] ISC-280: Make primary swaps the chosen address into \`users.email\` and the old primary into the additional list in one transaction
- [ ] ISC-281: After a primary change, member-facing email is addressed to the new primary
- [ ] ISC-282: A member signing in with an additional email resolves to their existing account, and no new users row is created
- [ ] ISC-283: OTP sign-in accepts an additional email
- [ ] ISC-284: A request submitted under an additional email attaches to the existing member, not an orphan
- [ ] ISC-285: Orphaned requests and member ownership checks match any of the member's emails
- [ ] ISC-286: Manual add of a member whose address is another member's additional email reuses that member
- [ ] ISC-287: The admin member search finds a member by an additional email
- [ ] ISC-288: Locker member resolution and auto-link match additional emails
- [ ] ISC-289: The member page shows every email with the primary marked, and add, remove and make-primary controls gated by the edit permission
- [ ] ISC-290: The merge preview returns both members, the counts of records that will move, and each membership field where the two differ
- [ ] ISC-291: Merge moves the duplicate's credentials, requests, confirmations, lockers, passkeys, notifications and audit entries to the kept member
- [ ] ISC-292: When both hold a membership in the club, the kept member's membership survives with role flags combined and blanks filled
- [ ] ISC-293: When both hold an admin assignment in the club, permissions are combined on the kept member's assignment
- [ ] ISC-294: The duplicate's primary and additional emails become additional emails of the kept member
- [ ] ISC-295: After a merge, signing in with the duplicate's old email reaches the kept member
- [ ] ISC-296: The duplicate's users row is deleted and a \`user_merges\` row records source and target
- [ ] ISC-297: A \`member_merged\` audit entry on the kept member carries the duplicate's snapshot and per-table moved counts
- [ ] ISC-298: Anti: merge is refused for self-merge, for the acting admin as the duplicate, and without the manage-admins permission
- [ ] ISC-299: Anti: merge is refused when either member has a membership or admin role in another club
- [ ] ISC-300: Anti: a failure partway through leaves both members exactly as they were (single transaction, both rows locked)
- [ ] ISC-301: A coverage test fails when a foreign key to \`users.id\`, or a unique index containing a user id column, is not handled by the merge
- [ ] ISC-302: User ids arriving from outside the database (payment metadata, session payloads) resolve through \`user_merges\`
- [ ] ISC-303: The member page has a Merge action opening a dialog with member search, the preview and a typed confirmation, then lands on the kept member
- [ ] ISC-304: Both audit renderers label the email-added, email-removed, primary-changed and member-merged actions
- [ ] ISC-305: Anti: adding emails, changing primary and merging send no email to anyone
- [ ] ISC-306: Typecheck, lint, drift and tests pass on the final tree, forced past the cache, with 0 skipped on the local Postgres

- [DEFERRED-VERIFY] ISC-309: Live: after release, the member page email controls and the merge dialog render in production (Interceptor); follow-up owed post-release
`;

s = s.slice(0, anchor).replace(/\n+$/, "\n") + crit + s.slice(anchor);

input.prompt:
Build two related features in AccessBuddy. Work ONLY in this git worktree (branch `feat/member-emails-and-merge`, cut from origin/main at v1.26.0): /home/nicholas-wood/Documents/workspace/projects/accessbuddy/.worktrees/member-emails-merge . Do not touch the other checkouts/worktrees, do not push, do not open a PR, do not touch production, GCP, Terraform or any remote database. Commit locally with conventional commits (`feat(members): ...`). Use bun (never npm). `fd` and `docker` are not installed; use rg/find. If any tool call (Write/Edit/Bash) is denied, stop and report the denial verbatim rather than retrying or working around it.

The request from Nick (owner): "can we have the ability to have multiple emails against a member, with one selected as primary. Also the ability to merge two member accounts together."

The criteria you are building to are ISC-269..ISC-308 in /home/nicholas-wood/Documents/workspace/projects/accessbuddy/ISA.md (section "### Member emails and member merge"); read that block and the 2026-11-22 Decisions entry first. Do not edit the ISA; report evidence per ISC and I will record it. Also read context/feedback.md in that project folder (quality bars: both audit renderers need labels; base-ui Select pattern; no surprise emails).

## Facts already established (verified inventory; trust but spot-check as you go)
- `users` (packages/db/src/schema/users.ts) is global, no RLS: `firebase_uid` UNIQUE NOT NULL, `email` text NOT NULL with NO unique constraint and NO index. Production may contain duplicate emails. Do not add any constraint or index to users.email.
- Three duplicate normalisers (`toLowerCase().trim()`): apps/web/src/lib/member-update-diff.ts:56, lib/services/locker-core.ts:68, lib/otp-store.ts:25.
- Sign-in mapping: apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts `getAuthUser` ~134-284: lookup by firebase_uid, fallback `eq(users.email, email)` then overwrites firebase_uid, else auto-creates a users row; then attaches orphan requests where `orphan_email = users.email`.
- Email lookups by exact match that must go through the new resolver: lib/auth.ts (fallback + getDevUserByEmail + orphan attach), app/api/auth/session/route.ts:62, app/api/auth/send-magic-link/route.ts:47, lib/services/magic-link.ts:52, app/api/auth/send-otp/route.ts:44, app/api/auth/verify-otp/route.ts:59, api/v1/t/[slug]/auth/send-code:48 and verify-code:58, members/route.ts POST:151 (dup check) and GET ilike search:40/49, members/lookup:40, admins/route.ts:78, platform/global-admins:60, requests/submit/route.ts:160 (and the 409 at 180 and locker session-email match at 148), lib/services/requests.ts:757-787 (orphan APPROVE), ownership-by-email checks (app/t/[slug]/dashboard/page.tsx:69, dashboard/requests/[id]/page.tsx:96, requests/[id]/member-cancel/route.ts:57, lib/services/confirm-receipt.ts:67), lockers (locker-core.ts resolveMember 304-334, linkLockerHoldersByEmail 345-411, lockers.ts 226-270 / 356-384 / 580-596, lockers/requests/[id]/cancel/route.ts:26, admin members/[id]/page.tsx:186). Line numbers are approximate; re-find each.
- Columns referencing users.id (all must be handled by merge): tenant_memberships.user_id [UNIQUE(tenant_id,user_id)], admin_assignments.user_id [UNIQUE(tenant_id,user_id)], fob_requests.{requester_id, exemption_reviewed_by, refunded_by, cancelled_by, approved_by, programmed_by, issued_by}, credentials.{owner_id, deactivated_by}, audit_log.actor_id, notifications.recipient_id, notification_preferences.user_id [UNIQUE(tenant_id,user_id,notification_type)], push_tokens.user_id, attestation_requests.{user_id, initiated_by}, webauthn_credentials.user_id (CASCADE), email_configurations.updated_by, reconciliations.uploaded_by, reconciliation_discrepancies.actioned_by, locker_requests.{user_id, decided_by}, locker_allocations.{user_id, allocated_by, ended_by}; no-FK: platform_settings.updated_by, audit_log.entity_id where entity_type='member', email_queue.entity_id where entity_type='member'. JSONB user ids inside audit_log.metadata are historical and are NOT rewritten.
- Member page: apps/web/src/app/t/[slug]/admin/members/[id]/page.tsx ([id] is the user id), form member-edit.tsx, PUT /api/v1/t/[slug]/members/[id] (permission APPROVE), archive uses MANAGE_ADMINS. Audit helper `createAuditEntry` in lib/services/audit.ts; fine-grained name goes in metadata.action; labels needed in BOTH components/audit-trail.tsx `describeAction` and app/t/[slug]/admin/audit/page.tsx `actionLabels`; existing test member-update-audit.test.ts.
- Migrations are hand-written SQL in packages/db/drizzle with a manual entry in meta/_journal.json (last is idx 21 `0021_lockers`, when 1786000060000). Avoid expression indexes (they break the drift check); store emails lower-cased and use a plain unique. schema-parity.test.ts and `bun run db:check-drift` must pass. If the new tables have no tenant_id they stay out of RLS_TABLES (check tenant-isolation.test.ts expectations).
- Tests: vitest, DB-gated on DATABASE_URL. A local Postgres is listening on 127.0.0.1:54329 (an embedded instance used by earlier work; the connection details and rebuild recipe are in ~/.claude/projects/-home-nicholas-wood--claude/memory/project-accessbuddy-pr125-force-renew-staging.md and the pr111 memory beside it). Use a fresh database on it for this branch; do not disturb databases other sessions may be using. Route-test pattern: apps/web/src/__tests__/lockers-routes.test.ts and helpers/locker-fixture.ts (mkTenant, mkUser, addMembership, addAdmin, cleanup).

## Design (decided; raise a flag in your report rather than silently deviating)

### A. Additional emails
1. Migration `0022_user_emails_and_merges.sql` + Drizzle schema + journal entry:
   - `user_alternate_emails(id uuid pk, user_id uuid not null FK users ON DELETE CASCADE, email text not null UNIQUE (stored lower-cased/trimmed), firebase_uid text UNIQUE NULL, created_by uuid NULL FK users ON DELETE SET NULL, created_at timestamptz not null default now())`, index on user_id.
   - `user_merges(source_id uuid pk (no FK; the row it names is deleted), target_id uuid not null FK users, merged_by uuid NULL FK users ON DELETE SET NULL, merged_at timestamptz not null default now())`.
   - Nothing touches `users`.
2. `users.email` remains THE primary; all existing reads stay as they are. One shared module (e.g. apps/web/src/lib/services/user-emails.ts) with: a single `normaliseEmail` (make the three existing ones re-export it), `findUserByEmail(dbOrTx, email)` (primary match first, case-insensitive on the stored value, deterministic order: earliest created; then additional-email match), `listUserEmails(userId)`, `userEmailSet(userId)` for "any of this member's emails" comparisons, plus add/remove/makePrimary services.
3. Replace the lookups listed above with the resolver so an additional email behaves like the primary for: Firebase sign-in fallback, OTP/code sign-in, request submission matching, orphan attach and ownership checks, manual-add duplicate check, admin/global-admin add by email, member lookup, member search (ilike over additional emails too), locker resolution/auto-link. Sign-in detail: when the Firebase uid is unknown and the email matches via an ADDITIONAL email, store the uid on that `user_alternate_emails.firebase_uid` row (do not overwrite users.firebase_uid, do not rename the member from displayName); uid lookup becomes users.firebase_uid first, then user_alternate_emails.firebase_uid. Sessions signed with users.firebase_uid keep working unchanged. No auto-create when any email matches.
4. API (same hand-rolled auth pattern as the sibling `members/[id]/*` routes, permission APPROVE, zod-validated, tenant membership of the target member verified):
   - `GET /api/v1/t/[slug]/members/[id]/emails` → `{primary, additional:[{id,email,createdAt}]}`
   - `POST .../emails {email}` → add. 400 invalid or already held by this member. If held (as primary or additional) by ANOTHER user: when that user has a membership in THIS tenant → 409 with `{code:"email_in_use", member:{id, firstName, lastName}}` so the UI can offer a merge; otherwise a generic 409 with no identifying detail.
   - `DELETE .../emails/[emailId]` → remove an additional email (primary cannot be removed; it is not a row).
   - `POST .../emails/[emailId]/make-primary` → one transaction: users.email := that address, old primary inserted as an additional row, the promoted row deleted. Do not move firebase uids around (the promoted row's uid, if any, must not be lost: carry it onto the new additional row for the old primary only if that is correct; think it through: uid→user resolution must still work for both addresses afterwards, and state your reasoning in the report).
   - Existing PUT members/[id] email edit: keep working, but reject (409, same scoping rule) when the new address belongs to another user, and if the new address is one of this member's own additional emails treat it as make-primary.
   - Audit each with entityType MEMBER, entityId the member, metadata.action `email_added` / `email_removed` / `primary_email_changed` (include the addresses). No emails are sent by any of these.
5. UI on the member page (in or beside MemberDetailsSection): an "Email addresses" list showing the primary with a Primary badge and each additional address with "Make primary" and "Remove" (confirm), plus an "Add email" input. Controls only when canEdit. On the in-use 409 show "This address belongs to <name>" with a "Merge members…" button when the viewer can merge. Follow existing component/styling conventions (shadcn on @base-ui/react, not Radix), mobile-safe, `router.refresh()` after mutations. Plain, short copy; no em dashes; Australian English.

### B. Merge
1. Service `mergeMembers({tenantId, targetUserId, sourceUserId, actor})` and `previewMerge(...)` (e.g. lib/services/member-merge.ts). Terminology in UI: the member whose page you are on is KEPT; the picked member is the DUPLICATE and is merged into it.
2. Guards (each a clear 4xx with a human message): permission MANAGE_ADMINS; target != source; source is not the acting admin; both have a membership in this tenant; neither has a membership or admin_assignment in any OTHER tenant and neither is a global admin (tenant_id NULL assignment) → refuse with "spans more than one club" (cross-club merge is out of scope). Do that cross-tenant check with the same DB access pattern `buildAuthContext` uses to load a user's memberships across tenants, and note in the report how it behaves once the app role stops bypassing RLS.
3. One DB transaction. `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` both users rows ordered by id. Then:
   - tenant_memberships collision (both in this tenant): keep the target row; OR the three role flags (keep the later of each expiry); fill target NULLs from source (accessLevelId, membershipNumber, membershipCategory, currentSeason: keep the later season string if both set, expiresAt: later); status ACTIVE if either is active; joinedAt earlier; delete the source row. The preview must list every field where the two differ and which value is kept.
   - admin_assignments collision: keep target row, union permissions, keep the higher role type (look at how roles rank in lib/permissions.ts); delete source row. Preview flags when the kept member gains permissions.
   - notification_preferences: repoint where no (tenant,type) collision, delete colliding source rows.
   - attestation_requests: move all; if both have a still-pending one for the same tenant/season/scope, look at the status model and cancel/expire the source's using the existing mechanism rather than leaving two live confirmations (explain what you chose).
   - Every other column in the inventory: UPDATE ... SET col = target WHERE col = source. Include audit_log.actor_id, audit_log.entity_id (entity_type member), email_queue.entity_id (entity_type member), platform_settings.updated_by, user_alternate_emails.created_by, user_merges.target_id/merged_by (earlier merges that pointed at the source must now point at the target), webauthn_credentials, push_tokens.
   - Emails: source primary + source additional emails become additional emails of the target (skip any the target already holds; lower-cased). Attach the source's users.firebase_uid to the row for the source's former primary so the next sign-in with that address resolves straight to the kept member (if the uid is a placeholder like `pending_…`, `pending:…`, `migrated_…`, store NULL instead).
   - Profile: keep target's name/phone/DOB, fill blanks from source.
   - Fob-request ownership that is keyed by email (orphan_email) needs no rewrite once the email set covers it; confirm with a test.
   - Insert user_merges(source,target,merged_by). DELETE the source users row LAST. If the delete (or anything) fails the whole transaction rolls back; map FK violations to a 409 "this member changed while merging, try again", never a 500 with half-applied state.
   - Audit: one entry on the target, entityType MEMBER, action UPDATE, metadata.action `member_merged`, with `source:{id, firstName, lastName, email, additionalEmails, firebaseUid, phone, membership snapshot, admin assignment snapshot}`, `moved:{<table.column>: count,...}`, and `membershipResolution` (the field decisions). No emails sent.
4. Outside-the-database ids: grep for places a user id arrives from outside and is looked up (Stripe PaymentIntent/checkout metadata, session/cookie payloads, tokens, links in emails, e.g. `/admin/members/<userId>` URLs).
